retention.stated: request-rate: MediaWiki edit-rate limits per IP; anon upload needs a CSRF token (probe returned `badtoken`). Retention: permanent, but Fandom never deletes content even on community request.

egress.terms: Unmetered, Cloudflare-fronted static CDN. But see the read-path trap below.

tooling: MediaWiki Action API per wiki (`action=upload`), Pywikibot/mwclient. No rclone backend.
chaining: 10 MB x unlimited files x unlimited free wikis (wiki creation is self-service). 10 MB is small enough that this only matters as a shard layer.

reliability_note: Two read-path traps in one host. (1) `static.wikia.nocookie.net` returns `403 Cf-Mitigated: challenge` to any non-browser. A hard read gate. (2) When it does serve, it RE-ENCODES: a request for a .png returned `Content-Type: image/webp`, 6,326 bytes, sha1 ada19fa5.. NOT the 9,979-byte original whose sha1 ce3dee8b.. matches the API. You must append `&format=original` to get your bytes back. Textbook 'gives you storage but not your bytes'.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: 'The maximum size of uploads is 10 MB ... There is no limit to the number of files you can upload'

probe: GET static.wikia.nocookie.net/.../Grass_Block.png/revision/latest (direct and via fetch proxy, browser UA) -> 403 with `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`; via proxy without UA -> 200 but image/webp 6,326 B, sha1 ada19fa5... != API sha1 ce3dee8b...
probe: same URL with `&format=original` -> 200, image/png, 9,979 bytes, sha1 ce3dee8bd03c3a66eedef6e710491cf9f4f11e2b == API sha1. Original IS retrievable, but only on the explicit original path.
